items.title: [Beekeeping365] One Cake a Day
items.content_html:
The story reflects on the significance of scarcity through a bakery that bakes only one cake daily. This practice embodies integrity and mindfulness, illustrating how the anticipation and appreciation of limited offerings can enhance their value. It draws parallels with beekeeping, emphasizing the importance of respecting nature's cycles and understanding what is within our control.

== Variations and related drinks ==

In addition to the UK and its former colonies, cider is popular in France (particularly [[Normandy]] and [[Brittany]]), Portugal (mainly in [[Entre-Douro-e-Minho Province|Minho]] and [[Madeira]]), northern Italy (specifically [[Friuli]]), and northern Spain (specifically [[Asturias]], [[Basque Country (greater region)|Basque Country]]). Due to fermentation, ciders can be thought of as a [[fruit wine]] made from apples, though the exact definitions of either beverage can vary by culture. Germany also has its own types of cider, with [[Rhineland-Palatinate]] and [[Hesse]] producing a particularly tart version known as [[Apfelwein]].


[[Calvados (brandy)|Calvados]] and [[Applejack (beverage)|applejack]] are strong liquors distilled from cider. items.title: [ahedderick.tumblr.com] Move-along Monday
items.content_html:
K went back to school last evening (Boy, I hope that chem test goes ok). I started off the morning a little slowly, but hope to get plenty done.

K and Aunt L and I picked all the remaining peppers in the garden yesterday. I processed the green bell and ‘banana-style’ peppers for the freezer yesterday with Aunt L, because she’s crazy about doing farm-ish chores. This morning I chopped about 3 dozen jalapeños for the freezer, and the few orange bell peppers we got. They take so darned long to turn from green to orange or yellow. I wore gloves for the jalapeños, and I still feel cautious about touching my face!

This morning I brought all the tomatoes worth saving in. I’ll puree them and . . figure something out. Dill, too, I have it in a bunch in a vase right now, and I’ll either dry it or chop and freeze. Who knows? Not me! But I am MAKING PROGRESS. Oh, one more thing; I planted a clove of elephant garlic in the asparagus bed. It has to be planted somewhere that is rich and won’t get tilled in the spring. When I see a strange leaf there in the spring, hopefully I’ll remember. It could happen.

Possibility of frost tomorrow morning. Any day, now, really.

The goats are tied in an area where they had already eaten all the low branches of the shrubs. I took pruning shears out and cut quite a few big, tall shrubs down and arranged them as a buffet. I kinda enjoyed it, on such a beautiful morning, but it was humid enough that I was sweating despite the cool temps. I don’t want to sweat any more. Augh!

Don’t touch your eyes don’t touch your eyes don’t touch

There’s business-y stuff I need to do, and I’m absolutely dreading it. As my brother and I take some needed last steps in dealing with our late father’s estate, I am having to coordinate with a lawyer, and possibly find a contractor to do “forensic estimation” of the value of old upgrades to the farm. I. Don’t. Wanna.

Also some pants (yes, they are foucking pamnts) to re-size. Cleanup from the weekend visitors. Moving along along along …
